newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cable & Wireless searches for China partner.
newsitem.headline: Cable & Wireless searches for China partner.

text.p: The ball is in the court of Cable & Wireless Plc in its search to find a strategic China partner without sacrificing its controlling shareholding in Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd, analysts said.

Following CITIC Pacific Ltd's decision to sell its 7.74 percent stake in Hongkong Telecom to a key Chinese company, the next move was up to C&W, which holds just over 59 percent of Hongkong Telecom, analysts said.
"It's not the end of the story -- it's the beginning of the story," said SBC Warburg analyst Jason Billings.
China Everbright, which is controlled by China's State Council, has a stake in China's second telephone network, China United Telecommunications Corp (China Unicom).
Since its establishment in 1994, China Unicom has been in bitter competition with the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications (MPT).
But Hongkong Telecom emphasised its good relations with MPT during a news briefing last week, one day before news of CITIC's divestment was released.
Analysts said Unicom had courted Hongkong Telecom for possible ventures, while Hongkong Telecom had been unsuccessfully courting MPT.
"From Hongkong Telecom's perspective, they're being dragged into this Unicom war (with MPT) on the wrong front," said Dylan Tinker, an analyst with Jardine Fleming Securities.

Analysts saw Friday's deal as the first step in a strategy to allow Hongkong Telecom to sidestep China's tough regime barring foreign telecoms from participating in its market, while allowing C&W to keep its majority stake.
They said the next move was probably up to Cable & Wireless now that CITIC Pacific, the utility's other major shareholder, had sold its stake.

Lisa Wong, an analyst at Mansion House Research, said investors believed that China Everbright might increase its stake in Hongkong Telecom, because 7.74 percent did not entitle it to a seat on the board.
Billings said C&W could sell down its stake to allow a mainland investor, probably China Unicom, to take a meaningful slice of Hongkong Telecom.
"C&W will most likely sell to a joint venture of (China) Unicom and China Everbright," said Billings.
Hongkong Telecom could join this joint venture either through buying in, or offering operational expertise, he said.
China Everbright's investment in Hongkong Telecom could be part of a State Council strategy to beef up China Unicom's challenge to MPT, analysts said.
Billings said one way C&W could retain a majority stake while allowing a mainland investor to buy more of Hongkong Telecom would be through a share buyback by Hongkong Telecom.
If C&W did not participate, its stake could rise as high as 66 percent, freeing it to sell 15 percent to a joint venture involving China Unicom and China Everbright, Billings said.
However, ING Barings investment analyst Nam Park was dubious that China would allow a foreign-owned utility into its telecom market.
